== Biography ==
James Glasgow was a cooper.

His death was indexed on 28 September 1860 in Pittsylvania County, Virginia, aged 71, supporting a birth about 1789. The original death register has not been inspected.<ref>"Virginia Deaths and Burials, 1853–1912," FamilySearch index, James Glasgow, 28 September 1860, Pittsylvania, Virginia, age 71, cooper, spouse Susan; FHL film 2048580. Also cited in Ancestry, Virginia, Deaths and Burials Index, 1853–1917.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Pittsylvania records and unproved parents — 23 October 2026 ===

The inspected [https://www.usgenwebsites.org/vagenweb/pittsylvania/deaths/1860Deaths.htm USGenWeb 1860 Pittsylvania death transcription] records James Glasgow, cooper, age 71 years 10 months 12 days, Pittsylvania birthplace, cause '''“killed,”''' and Susan Glasgow as informant and wife. Its parent column and exact death-date cell are blank. This is a modern transcription of county returns; the original register was not inspected. The existing 28 September 1860 date comes from the previously cited death index, FHL 2048580. Combining that date with the transcribed age yields 16 November 1788; this is a calculated birthday, not independent birth evidence, so the approximate birth field is retained.

The [https://www.usgenwebsites.org/vagenweb/pittsylvania/marriages/1767marriage.pdf#page=104 marriage-bond compilation], printed p. 101/PDF p. 104, visually checked 23 October, gives James Glasgow/Susanna High, 21 October 1818, with Freeman High bondsman and no James parent. Printed p. 83/PDF p. 86 lists Robert Glasgow as bondsman for the 22 December 1815 Eudaley/Glasgow marriage. The original review below supersedes that role: Herod Worsham was surety, while Robert Glasgow signed a separate age-and-willingness declaration. The declaration remains a local associated lead, not an established father or proved brother/sister link. The compilation is not the original bond. The 1818 original has since been inspected, as described in the 30 October source review below; the 1815 family-identification test remains open.

A [https://www.ancestry.com/genealogy/records/james-glasgow-24-1csrc5 contributed Ancestry aggregation] names Robert Glasgow 1760–1839 and Sarah Cooper 1763–1853 as parents, without an inspected supporting record. No named parent is selected from this claim. [[Glasgow-1530|Robert-1530]] has matching years but is a documented Glasgow weaver with Jack/Brash marriages; he is not identified by a year match. [[Glasgow-12|Robert-12]], the Ohio immigrant with different wives, remains unconnected to this household. [[Glasgow-395|Robert-395]] is specifically inconsistent: his son James was already dead in a 1837 newspaper account, whereas this cooper lived to 1860. [[Glasgow-357|William-357]] and his Sarah Cooper 1756–1812 are a different Currituck couple; neither can be renamed or imported to fill this gap. The 1815 bond may help identify a local family, but does not establish the contributed Robert/Sarah couple.

=== Possible Danville deposition — 27 October 2026 ===

An original deposition names '''James Glasgow''' at the National Hotel in Danville on '''8 April 1840'''. He states that in 1836 he heard Armistead G. Weir say that he had purchased fodder from James M. Sutherlin; he thought it was two stacks and gave an opinion of their value. The page bears a signature reading James Glasgow. He is a witness, not a stated buyer or seller.<ref>Library of Virginia, Pittsylvania County chancery case 1841-001, James M. Sutherlin and wife v. Armistead G. Weir; [https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/143-Pittsylvania/Box041/143_1841_001_0021.pdf image 21, James Glasgow deposition], and [https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/143-Pittsylvania/Box041/143_1841_001_0022.pdf image 22, attestation], 8 April 1840. Caption spells the defendant's surname Wier. Original images visually inspected 27 October 2026.</ref>

The name and locality make this a compatible candidate for the Pittsylvania cooper, but the deposition gives no age, occupation, residence, spouse or parents to prove the identification. The following Roderick R. Hudnall testimony is a separate witness's answer. The separate Virginia-born [[Glasgow-193|James M. Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-2925|James William Glasgow]] have Ohio and Tennessee household accounts; geography alone does not exclude travel to Danville. This source establishes no new parent or exact vital date for the profile.

=== Original marriage bond checked — 30 October 2026 ===

The original bond confirms that James Glasgow obtained a licence to marry Susanah High on 21 October 1818. James Glasgow and Freeman High are the obligors; James signs his name and Freeman’s entry bears his mark. R. Hopkins is the witness. No parent, age or occupation of James is stated.<ref>Pittsylvania County, Virginia, original marriage bonds, 1816–1820, FamilySearch DGS 007741064, item 3 (1818), [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C91C-YQ6X-J image 270 of 281, James Glasgow/Susanah High bond], 21 October 1818; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C91C-YQCW-C preceding endorsement, image 269]. Original images visually inspected 30 October 2026; bond image downloaded.</ref> This confirms the earlier compilation, without establishing James’s father, Freeman’s kinship to the bride, or the identity of the 1840 deponent.

=== Original 1815 roles and signature comparison — 30 October 2026 ===

The original 22 December 1815 bond names Robert Eudaley and Herod Worsham as obligors; both signature entries bear marks. Robert Glasgow instead signed the separate declaration that Elizabeth was of age and willing to marry. The typed compilation’s Robert Glasgow bondsman entry is contradicted by the original bond. Neither original states that Robert was Elizabeth’s father or that Elizabeth was James’s sister.<ref>Pittsylvania County, Virginia, original marriage bonds, FamilySearch DGS007741063, item2: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C91C-R33H-Y bond front, full-film image311/item image175]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C91C-R33H-2 endorsement, image310]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C91C-R334-N Robert Glasgow declaration, image309/item image173]. Originals visually inspected30October2026; compared with the typed compilation, printed83/PDF86.</ref> The declaration gives no exact age or literal kin term.

A non-expert visual comparison of the original1818 and1840 James Glasgow signatures finds compatible broad cursive features, without a diagnostic family, age or occupational identifier. It is not handwriting authentication. The1840 deponent remains a compatible candidate; James’s parents remain unknown.


=== Little Fall Creek witness network — 30 October 2026 ===

The original depositions taken at the Exchange Hotel in Danville on 1 October 1851 name James Glasgow and William Glasgow. James says he was a neighbour of Leonard Fitzgerald in 1821 and recalls renting part of the Little Fall Creek property around 1826 through an agent. William separately says he was Fitzgerald’s neighbour in 1821 and thinks Fitzgerald remained there in 1827, while expressly not being positive. Both signatures appear. The testimony gives neither Glasgow man’s age, occupation, spouse or parents and does not call the two men relatives.<ref>Library of Virginia, Pittsylvania chancery1854-055, James Lanier v. Anderson Kirby etc., depositions taken1October1851: [https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/143-Pittsylvania/Box070/143_1854_055_0023.pdf scan23, opening/date], [https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/143-Pittsylvania/Box070/143_1854_055_0024.pdf scan24] and [https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/143-Pittsylvania/Box070/143_1854_055_0025.pdf scan25, James’s testimony], [https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/143-Pittsylvania/Box070/143_1854_055_0026.pdf scan26, James’s signature and William’s testimony/signature]. Original manuscript scans visually inspected30October2026.</ref>

James Glasgow-62, the Pittsylvania cooper, is the leading existing compatible candidate for the James deponent, not a proved identification. Same county, sustained local knowledge and the existing1840deponent comparison support investigation; no family identifier links them. William’s identity and any kinship with James, the1815declarant Robert or Elizabeth remain unresolved. No duplicate person, father candidate, parent attachment, vital change or confidence gain is created.

The original1850Danville census, enumerated5November, records the existing household: James61, cooper; Susan57; Susan20; Berryman18, cooper; James D.12; Obediah11. It does not state their relationships or James’s parents. This confirms the already cited census household, not a new birth date or parent.<ref>1850United States census, Danville, Pittsylvania County, Virginia, printed p.320, household4, lines20–25; FamilySearch DGS004206390,item2,image186, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-DYLN-TC original image]. Inspected30October2026. The index’s line-number field differs from the printed schedule.</ref>
